operating_rules: Submit one prompt at a time and stop at its checkpoint.
Propose first, review, then apply. Authoring and execution are separate prompts.
Before each cloud operation, state the provider, server and actual tool used.
For steps assigned to Fabric MCP, call that server's tool directly. Do not substitute REST, Azure CLI or a skill that calls APIs. If the tool is unavailable, report the limitation and stop.
Check for an existing item before creating one, and before retrying any write.
Never print tokens or enable token-bearing debug output.
Use exact workspace, lakehouse and model IDs (kept in local notes only) for every write.

Use the guide's Fabric MCP profile hc01-lab (this folder's .mcp.json; for VS Code run ffia mcp render hc01-lab --client vscode --output <LAB_PATH>/.vscode/mcp.json). It exposes only the tools steps 02-05 name, and every write needs approval.
os_constraints: Power BI Desktop preview and publish steps need Windows. Other steps run on Windows, macOS or Linux.

summary: A fictional manufacturer's sales lands in a Fabric lakehouse. A read-only Fabric data agent answers governed questions. A Foundry agent uses it as a tool to answer questions and write monthly team briefs, adds cited public context through web grounding, and explains data-quality issues while a data steward approves any fix applied upstream in Silver. Portal, code-first and offline paths.
tenant_settings: A Fabric F2+ capacity (or P1+) for the lakehouse and the data agent.
Users can use Copilot and other features powered by Azure OpenAI (required by the data agent).
Fabric data agent, its data sources and the Foundry project in the same tenant; data sources on same-region capacities.
title: MFG-01: Foundry agents + Fabric for sales insights (manufacturing, synthetic)
